# Independent audit: actual smooth singleton menu with insufficient convex-field efficiency

Audited `candidate 30917746e40e143c` in full. The exact construction and all stated bounds pass.

The base triangle has exactly its three vertices and the origin as lattice points; the displayed inequalities give the claimed enumeration at the four possible coordinate sums. Its product with a positive triangle is a full-dimensional convex body with four identical positive fibers.

The all-ambient depth certificate is valid. For any base tilt and any nonzero continuous normal, cyclic barycentric copies of one uniform triangle point have continuous sum 3g, and the three outer base vectors sum to zero. The total buffered margin is strictly positive. At least one of the three kernel values is consequently exactly one, so expected total outer capture is at least V, without any restriction on obliqueness. A finite exposing tilt attains precisely V plus the selected own-fiber capture. Closed pure-base caps cost at least 2V and therefore do not lower the resulting Q=V+q. Exposure at the outer vertices similarly identifies their own depths. Strict own-fiber H concavity and proper smooth cap attainment justify uniqueness of the middle maximizing mark.

The cyclic minimizing continuous normals have sum zero under the dual affine symmetry, preserve the covariance normalization, and have equal smooth coareas. Their three base forms give values 2,-1,-1 on the vertices, so one common finite large tilt makes all outer transition slabs empty with exactly one full outer fiber per cap. Thus all three caps are actually minimizing at the unique deepest mark, their equal response weights are justified, and every kernel base centroid is exactly zero. The outer boundary profile is exactly 1/3, not only asymptotically.

For the continuous triangle, a one-vertex centroid cut has intercepts satisfying 1/alpha+1/beta=3 and alpha,beta<=1. Its area fraction ranges from 4/9 to 1/2, with its unique minimum at alpha=beta=2/3. Complementary two-vertex cuts therefore have fraction at least 1/2. This verifies the complete three-element ordinary minimizing-normal set and the convergence of the smoothed minimizing directions to that set.

On an edge the canonical profile is 1/3 plus one third of the indicator of its middle third. Integrating the midpoint convexity inequality gives middle-third convex mass at most one third of total convex mass. The perturbation is confined to interior edge bands of length tending to zero. Jensen on a centered interval of length 1/2 bounds every nonnegative convex test there by twice its full edge integral. Thus the error estimate is uniform over the ENTIRE convex field cone, including steep tests; it is not an invalid use of unweighted convergence against unbounded varying tests. One may take eta to be the maximum of the normalized error-band lengths over the three edges.

Finally Jensen at the origin in base space gives R>=3I_0. Since 4/9+2eta>1/3, the ratio [(4/9+2eta)I_0+R/3]/(I_0+R) is maximized at R=3I_0, giving 13/36+eta/2. The case I_0=0 gives efficiency 1/3 directly; zero total field integral is irrelevant. A constant field attains 13/36 in the limit. The strict gap below 4/9 for eta<1/6 is correct.

This certificate does not contradict OC: its normalized depth tends to 13/36, greater than Gamma_2/4=1/9. It also does not contradict the newly audited exposed-complete-base theorem, because its unique source is interior to the complete base triangle. It rigorously rules out a universal individual Gamma_d convex-field credit for every actual smooth singleton menu, even with global deepestness and exact smooth kernel centroids. Attained bad-body stationarity or favorable-menu selection is additional information absent from the certificate.
